numberItems.stem: The handbook says safe CMV operation requires skill in how many basic control areas (accelerating, steering, stopping and backing safely)?
numberItems.explanation: Safe operation of a CMV requires skill in 4 areas: accelerating, steering, stopping and backing safely (p. 2-9).

numberItems.stem: How many simple safe-backing rules does the handbook list (proper position, look at your path, both mirrors, back slowly, driver's side, helper)?
The handbook's basic method for a double-clutch upshift has how many steps?
numberItems.explanation: The double-clutch upshift (and downshift) method is listed in 5 steps, from releasing the accelerator and clutching into Neutral to releasing the clutch and pressing the accelerator (pp. 2-10 to 2-11).

numberItems.stem: The handbook describes 2 ways of knowing when to shift up. What are they?
options: Engine temperature and oil pressure
Retarder setting and road grade
Engine speed (rpm) and road speed (mph)
numberItems.explanation: There are 2 ways of knowing when to shift: engine speed (rpm) on the tachometer and road speed (mph) on the speedometer (p. 2-11).

numberItems.stem: The handbook names 2 special times when you should downshift. What are they?
options: Before starting down a hill, and before entering a curve
Once you feel the truck speed up on a hill, and in the middle of a curve
Before backing, and before stopping at a light
numberItems.explanation: Downshift before starting down a hill and before entering a curve (p. 2-11).

numberItems.stem: How many basic types of retarders are there, according to the handbook?
options: 2: engine and exhaust
4: exhaust, engine, hydraulic and electric
5: exhaust, engine, hydraulic, electric and air
numberItems.explanation: There are 4 basic types of retarders: exhaust, engine, hydraulic and electric (p. 2-11).

numberItems.stem: When a retarder is turned on, where does it apply its braking power?
options: To all wheels, whenever you press the brake pedal
To the trailer wheels only
To the drive wheels only, whenever you let up on the accelerator all the way
numberItems.explanation: Retarders apply braking power to the drive wheels only, whenever you let up on the accelerator pedal all the way (p. 2-11).

numberItems.stem: When should you turn your retarder off?
options: Whenever the road is wet, icy or snow-covered
Whenever you go down a long, steep grade
Never, because it helps prevent skids on slippery roads
numberItems.explanation: When the drive wheels have poor traction the retarder may cause them to skid, so turn it off whenever the road is wet, icy or snow covered (p. 2-11).

numberItems.stem: Which gear should you use when you back up?
options: The highest reverse gear
The lowest reverse gear
Neutral, letting the vehicle coast back
numberItems.explanation: Back as slowly as possible using the lowest reverse gear, so you can correct steering errors and stop quickly (p. 2-10).

numberItems.stem: When you have to back and turn, which direction is safest?
options: Toward the right side, so traffic stays away from you
Toward the driver's side
Toward whichever side is closer to the dock
numberItems.explanation: Back and turn toward the driver's side so you can see better, even if it means going around the block (p. 2-10).

numberItems.stem: Before you back with a helper, you work out hand signals. Which signal does the handbook say you must agree on?
options: "Stop"
"Turn left"
"Slow down"
numberItems.explanation: Work out a set of hand signals you both understand and agree on a signal for "stop" (p. 2-10).

numberItems.stem: When backing a vehicle with a trailer, which way do you turn the steering wheel?
options: Toward the direction you want the trailer to go
Keep it straight until the trailer starts to turn
In the opposite direction from where you want the trailer to go
numberItems.explanation: Backing a car, straight truck or bus: turn toward where you want to go. Backing a trailer: turn the wheel in the opposite direction (p. 2-10).

numberItems.stem: Before starting down a steep hill, what gear should you be in?
options: The same gear you used to climb the hill
Usually a lower gear than you would need to climb the same hill
One gear higher than the climbing gear
numberItems.explanation: Be in a low enough gear, usually lower than the gear required to climb the same hill (p. 2-11).

numberItems.stem: You drive a vehicle with an automatic transmission down a grade. What should you do?
options: Select a low range to get greater engine braking
Shift to Neutral to save fuel
Select the highest range so the engine does not over-rev
numberItems.explanation: With an automatic, select a low range to get greater engine braking on downgrades (p. 2-11).

numberItems.stem: Some newer vehicles use "progressive" shifting. What does that mean?
options: The shift rpm stays the same in every gear
The shift rpm gets lower as you move up through the gears
The shift rpm gets higher as you move up through the gears
numberItems.explanation: With progressive shifting, the rpm at which you shift becomes higher as you move up in the gears (p. 2-11).
